assertions.exact_claim: The planar $(1+N)$-body problem describes the coorbital limit of central configurations with one dominant mass~\cite{CLN}. Its geometry and stability have been studied in~\cite{Moeckel94,RS}; results for four satellites include the equal-mass classification~\cite{AF,CLO}, stacked configurations~\cite{OC}, and mass symmetries~\cite{DHW}. For three satellites, Corbera, Cors and Llibre~\cite{CCL} and Corbera, Cors, Llibre and Moeckel~\cite{CCLM} describe the bifurcations of relative equilibria. In particular, \cite[Theorem~2]{CCLM} gives convex uniqueness for every fixed positive mass ratio and sufficiently small total satellite mass.
assertions.proof_route_note: Prior literature overview. No result in this paragraph is a proof input. The AF chamber seed actually used below is independently proved; the unrelated three-satellite classification is outside the requested substantive proof scope.

assertions.exact_claim: The proof first establishes convex coorbital uniqueness. Uniformity then requires control when some $\mu_i$ tend to zero and satellites coalesce. Following the cluster approach of~\cite{Moeckel}, we classify these limits, regularize their equations, and connect every small-mass convex configuration to its coorbital limit. The signed-area estimates ensure that this continuation remains convex without imposing a relation between the mass parameter and the collision scales.

assertions.source_text:
A second complete pair would also have vanishing total mass, which is impossible. The exterior angular equations therefore give separation $h$. The pair's weighted $T$-average, divided by $\nu$ after internal cancellation, gives the probe equation. Finally divide \eqref{eq:pair-qdiff} by $\delta$: its radial contribution tends to zero, its angular derivative tends to $D$, and its right side is $\nu/d^3+o(1)$. Lemma~\ref{lem:probe} gives $D>0$.
\end{proof}

assertions.source_text: Since $DF_0\to3e(\psi)e(\psi)^T$, radial differences between groups are $o(d)$, and the same holds within groups. Equation~\eqref{eq:distance} now gives $W/d\to1$.

assertions.exact_claim:
If $\nu/d^3\to0$, repeat these normalized averages in the angular equations. Cross-group interactions are $O(\nu/d^2)=o(d)$, and each averaged $J$ differs from its representative value by $o(d)$. Subtraction, \eqref{eq:triple-J}, and the radial estimate give $D_0(\varphi_i-\varphi_j)=o(d)$, contradicting distinct scaled groups. This proves the lower bound. Reflection gives the other endpoint block.
\end{proof}

assertions.exact_claim:

The triple estimates imply $K=\omega d^{-2}(1+o(1))$ and $J_0-J_c=-D_0\omega d+o(d)$. Division by $\omega d$ gives $\nu/d^3\to D_0$, hence $\mu_c/d^3\to D_0$. Now $H_v\to3D_0$ in \eqref{eq:nested-derivatives}; dividing the pair angular difference by $\delta$, with $\Delta\rho/\delta=O(\eps)$, gives $\xi/s^3\to3D_0$. All averages use current normalized masses, so the conclusions hold on the selected fixed-label sequence.
\end{proof}

assertions.exact_claim:
For fixed $\eps\ne0$ and, in the nested chart, $\eta>0$, substitute
$q_i(t)=q^0+tb_i+O(t^2)$ and $\mu_i=t^3\omega_i$ in the Cartesian equations, keeping $q_p=ae(0)$ fixed.
Their first-order terms are $t$ times the left side of \eqref{eq:vector-slow}; the exterior mass and reaction vector change only at order $t^3$.
On these paths $Y-c_\eps X=O(t^3)$, and the exact identities
\[
 R_i=[F_i+\eps(Y-c_\eps X)]\cdot e(\varphi_i),\qquad
 T_i=\frac{\rho_i}{\eps}[F_i+\eps(Y-c_\eps X)]\cdot e^\perp(\varphi_i)
\]
identify the boundary difference rows with the radial projections and $a/\eps$ times the tangential projections. Basis derivatives contribute nothing because $F(q^0)=0$; the center and exterior rows vanish on the background.
Thus \eqref{eq:vector-slow} solves these boundary equations. Their joint smooth extensions from Section~\ref{sec:charts} also give the identities at zero parameters.

assertions.proof_route: The new defect is genuinely relativeField - inverse(1+epsilon) relativeAverage. Fixed exterior cancellation yields an exact t^3 factor and a continuous bounded coefficient on both actual charts, without a root premise. assertions.source_text:
For fixed $\eps\ne0$ and, in the nested chart, $\eta>0$, substitute
$q_i(t)=q^0+tb_i+O(t^2)$ and $\mu_i=t^3\omega_i$ in the Cartesian equations, keeping $q_p=ae(0)$ fixed.
Their first-order terms are $t$ times the left side of \eqref{eq:vector-slow}; the exterior mass and reaction vector change only at order $t^3$.
On these paths $Y-c_\eps X=O(t^3)$, and the exact identities
\[
 R_i=[F_i+\eps(Y-c_\eps X)]\cdot e(\varphi_i),\qquad
 T_i=\frac{\rho_i}{\eps}[F_i+\eps(Y-c_\eps X)]\cdot e^\perp(\varphi_i)
\]
identify the boundary difference rows with the radial projections and $a/\eps$ times the tangential projections. Basis derivatives contribute nothing because $F(q^0)=0$; the center and exterior rows vanish on the background.
Thus \eqref{eq:vector-slow} solves these boundary equations. Their joint smooth extensions from Section~\ref{sec:charts} also give the identities at zero parameters.

\end{proposition}
